  .sc-cookie-banner-actions > * {

If you are a task openapi v1 user and want to switch to v2, you need to reapply for new scopes and complete the publishing process.</p><p>To make it easier to distinguish, the names of v1 openapi scopes are marked with suffix "historical version".</p></blockquote><p>To apply scopes, go to the “Permissions & Scopes” page of the application development console and search for the corresponding scopes.<span class="img-viewer-container"><img alt="image.png" class="img-viewer-consumer" src="//sf16-sg.larksuitecdn.com/obj/open-platform-opendoc-sg/8bdf70df8d36d88cd9ebd26858e5847e_uirEZlkM89.png?height=1384&lazyload=true&width=2562"></span></p><p>For Custom Apps (enterprise built-in apps), the enterprise administrator needs to approve the application in the Lark Admin Console; for Store Apps, the platform administrator needs to review and approve the application, and the enterprise administrator needs to install or upgrade the application in the app market. Apply for access_token with calling identity</h3><p>To invoke some API, you must apply an access_token which indicates the <strong>calling identity</strong>. Lark tasks will perform specific authorization based on the calling identity.</p><p>Task API supports <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> and <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code>.</p><div class="md-table_table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Type</th><th>tenant_access_token</th><th>user_access_token</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Description</td><td>Invoke the task api with the application identity, and perform CRUD operations on the task data created by the application.</td><td>Invoke the task api with the user identity, which is equivalent to the user directly operating the Lark App task user interface.</td></tr><tr><td>Use case</td><td>Use this token when the application needs to have its own task data. For example:<br>In a project management application, you need to create tasks for project members. You can use <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> to create tasks with the application identity and add specific users as task owners.</td><td>Users develop third-party task applications, using Lark's identity information and Lark task capabilities, but want to provide a different user interface from Lark.</td></tr><tr><td>Acquisition method</td><td>The application can directly obtain the tenant_access_token through the app_id and app_secret from Lark's open platform authorization interface.</td><td>Guide users to log in to Lark, and then obtain the user_access_token under user authorization.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>The calling identity of <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> and <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> are both "users" from the perspective of the task system interal, and both have names, avatars, and other attributes, and will by authorized in the same way. In other words, <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> <strong>has NO special privileges</strong> and cannot access the task data belonging to other users or other applications, nor can it be used as the "tenant administrator" role. The difference between <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> and <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> is simply how they are acquired: <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> requires a real user's authorization to generate; while <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> does not require it and can be applied directly through the application's appid/secret.</p><blockquote><p>Both <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> and <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> have expiration. Normally, it is about 2 hours. Formal applications need to implement a component to re-generate new access tokens periodically to ensure the application can always use a valid access token.</p><p>For more information, please refer to <a href="/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM" class="internal-link" target="_self">Get access token</a>.</p></blockquote><h3 id="c64056d" tabindex="-1">3. Invoke APIs</h3><p>After completing the above two steps, you can now invoke the apis. You can view the api documentation to obtain the domain name and URL information of the interface, and pass the access_token mentioned above in the form of <code class="md-render_code-inline">Authorization</code> Header (the token should be prefixed with "Bearer "). For example:</p><pre class="hljs"><div class="copy-btn"><svg fill="currentColor" width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" fill-rule="evenodd"><rect x="4" y="7" width="9" height="9" rx="1"></rect><path d="M8 4h7a1 1 0 011 1v7" stroke-linecap="round"></path></g></svg></div><code class="md-render_code-block"><div><div class="hljs-line" start="1">POST <api url></div><div class="hljs-line" start="2"></div><div class="hljs-line" start="3">Authorization: Bearer <access_token></div><div class="hljs-line" start="4"></div><div class="hljs-line" start="5"><req body></div></div></code></pre><p>For example, apply for a <code class="md-render_code-inline">tenant_access_token</code> and invoke the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/create" class="internal-link" target="_self">Create Task</a> api to create a task. Then use the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/add_members" class="internal-link" target="_self">Add Task Members</a> api to add your user (represented by the user's open id) as the task assignee. The task should now also appear in the "My Owned" task list in Lark Task.</p><p>Afterwards, you can switch to <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> of yourself to invoke the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/get" class="internal-link" target="_self">Get Task Details</a> api to view the details of the task. Since the current user is the task assignee, they have permission to get the details of it. Then try to use another user' <code class="md-render_code-inline">user_access_token</code> to invoke the same api to get the same task details, and you will get an error code of 1470403, because that user is not a member of the task and cannot access the task.</p><h2 id="1de75e51" tabindex="-1">Task Terminology and Concepts</h2><p>To effectively use the api, it is necessary to understand some task terminology and concepts.</p><ul class="md_render-table_solid md_render-table"><li><strong>Task</strong>: A task records a user's to-do item. It has properties such as summary, description, and whether it is completed, etc. Each task has a globally unique ID, or <strong>Task GUID</strong> with which you can manipulate it through api.</li><li><strong>Subtask</strong>: A sub task belonging to a task, generally used for work breakdown. A task can have multiple subtasks, and subtasks can also have their own subtasks. Apart from having a reference to a parent task, subtasks are no different from normal tasks.</li><li><strong>Task Assignee</strong>: Each task can have several assignees. The assignee can modify the task and mark it as completed, etc. According to the principle of "one person responsible for one thing", it is recommended that a task should have only one assignee, but the system does not enforce this.</li><li><strong>Task Follower</strong>: Each task can have several followers. Followers can receive notifications when task is changed. Task assignees and followers are collectively referred to as Task Members. A user can be an assignee and a follower simultaneously in the same task.</li><li><strong>Task Completion Mode</strong>: When a task has multiple assignees, it can be set to either of two modes: "Or-Sign Task" - when any assignee marks the task as completed, the entire task is completed; "Countersign Task" - when all assignees mark the task as completed, the entire task is considered completed.</li><li><strong>My Tasks</strong>: The collection of tasks for which the user is the assignee. They are displayed in the "Owned" UI of the Lark App Task Center.</li><li><strong>Tasklist</strong>: It is a container for a group of tasks. It is used for organizing, managing, and tracking the progress of tasks related to a single project. Each tasklist also has a globally unique Tasklist ID (abbreviated as Tasklist GUID) for API operations.</li><li><strong>Tasklist Owner</strong>: Each list has one user with management permissions for the list. When a list is created, the creator is the owner of the tasklist. The owner can transfer ownership to other users, but the owner cannot be absent. Only the tasklist owner can change the owner, and only the owner can delete the tasklist.</li><li><strong>Tasklist Member</strong>: Each tasklist can have multiple members. Members can be either users or chats. Members can have "viewer" or "editor" roles. "Viewer" member can view the tasklist and the tasks in the tasklist; "editor" members can modify the tasklist name, add or remove tasks from the tasklist, adjust the task order, etc. A user can only have one role in the same tasklist.</li><li><strong>Comment</strong>: Comments can be made on tasks to record information related to the task. Comments can be updated or deleted by the comment creator.</li><li><strong>Section</strong>：Sections can be defined in "My Tasks" and tasklist by which user can categorize their tasks manually.</li><li><strong>Custom Field</strong>: Each tasklist can be added several custom fields(number, member, datetime, single_select, multi_select). Task in such tasklists can be set custom field values.</li><li><strong>Attachment</strong>: Each task can attach multiple files, such as images, PDF documents or zip files, etc. These files can be previewed or downloaded by the task members.</li></ul><p>Note: The Task API v2 adjusts some terminology for the Task v1 API.</p><ul class="md_render-table_solid md_render-table"><li>The task GUID is referred to "task ID" in v1 api. And in the v2 API, the term "task GUID" is always used to refer to the globally unique ID of a task, such as <code class="md-render_code-inline">df8a7aff-18c1-4b9c-9959-0dda10c49309</code>; task ID is used to refer to the multi-digit numerical ID starting with "t" generated for each task (e.g., <code class="md-render_code-inline">t1002325</code>).</li><li>The task assignee is referred to as "collaborator" in the v1 api 。</li></ul><h2 id="229c10e9" tabindex="-1">API Design Principles and Specifications</h2><h3 id="771a4ef6" tabindex="-1">API Style</h3><p>The whole API adopts the Restful-like style. Each core business concept is designed as a resource, including: "task", "tasklist", "comment", etc. The regular creation, retrieval of details, retrieval of lists, updates, and deletion of resources all use the Restful style. For example, for a task, the main operations are designed as follows:</p><div class="md-table_table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Operation</th><th>HTTP Method</th><th>HTTP URL</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Create Task</td><td>POST</td><td>/task/v2/tasks</td></tr><tr><td>View Task Detail</td><td>GET</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid</td></tr><tr><td>Get Task List</td><td>GET</td><td>/task/v2/tasks</td></tr><tr><td>Update Task</td><td>PATCH</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid</td></tr><tr><td>Delete Task</td><td>DELETE</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>For other non-standard Restful APIs, for write apis, use <code class="md-render_code-inline">POST</code> and add the action name after the resource ID in the URL. Such as:</p><div class="md-table_table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Operation</th><th>HTTP Method</th><th>HTTP URL</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Add Task Members</td><td>POST</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid/add_members</td></tr><tr><td>Remove Task from List</td><td>POST</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid/remove_tasklist</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>For read apis, use the <code class="md-render_code-inline">GET</code> method and add the sub-resource to be obtained after the resource ID in the URL. Such as:</p><div class="md-table_table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Operation</th><th>HTTP Method</th><th>HTTP URL</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Get All Lists of a Task</td><td>GET</td><td>/task/v2/tasks/:task_guid/tasklists</td></tr><tr><td>Get Task List in a List</td><td>GET</td><td>/task/v2/tasklists/:tasklist_guid/tasks</td></tr></tbody></table></div><h2 id="be3382e1" tabindex="-1">About Resource Update</h2><p>In the Restful style, resource updates can use PUT (whole update) or PATCH (partial update). In the Task API, PATCH (partial update) is always used. The advantage of partial update is that the caller can accurately specify which field to update without worrying about accidentally cleaning the corresponding data due to forgetting to fill in some fields. At the same time, using the partial update style can clearly distinguish between "not update a field" and "clean a field".</p><p>To support partial updates, the update api request normally includes a resource field and an <code class="md-render_code-inline">update_fields</code> field . <code class="md-render_code-inline">update_fields</code> is used to declare which fields to update. The data of resource fields declare what data should be changed to. For example, for the update task api:</p><pre class="hljs"><div class="copy-btn"><svg fill="currentColor" width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" For example, to update a task, but without the edit permission of the task.</td><td>You need to query the permission section of the relevant API documentation to confirm that the caller has the permission.</td></tr><tr><td>404</td><td>1470404</td><td>The resource requested does not exist or has been deleted. If the problem persists after multiple retries, please contact the support staff to report the problem. <br> Please provide the logid and request parameters when submitting feedback.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>For 400 errors, because they are numerous and most of them can be discovered and solved during development, generally they share the same code in order to avoid introducing too many fragmented error codes. For example:</p><div class="md-table_table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Error Scenario</th><th>Error Message</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>When creating a task, the <code class="md-render_code-inline">due</code> parameter is set, but the required <code class="md-render_code-inline">timestamp</code> is not provided.</td><td>Invalid Param 'due.timestamp', param is required.</td></tr><tr><td>When adding a task member, the role is neither "assignee" nor "follower"</td><td>Invalid Param 'members', role is invalid. Only 'assignee', 'follower' are supported.</td></tr><tr><td>Invoke the Update Task API, set the task repeat rule, but the task has no due.<br> The repeat rule can only be set for tasks with due.</td><td>Invalid Param 'repeat_rule', cannot set repeat_rule without setting due.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>For some special cases, additional specific error codes are defined to help developers write correct error handling codes. For example, each task supports only one reminder. When using the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/add_reminders" class="internal-link" target="_self">Add Task Reminder</a> api to add more than one reminder to a task, you will get an error code of 1470613. In this way, developers can develop logic to remove the existing reminder first by calling the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/remove_reminders" class="internal-link" target="_self">Remove Task Reminder</a> api.</p><p><strong>We very much welcome developers to provide feedbacks on the return of errors, to improve the quality of error message, or add necessary error codes for specific scenarios</strong>.</p><h2 id="5dbccd6c" tabindex="-1">Pagination API Convention</h2><p>Some API (such as the <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/tasklist/tasks" class="internal-link" target="_self">Get Task List</a> interface) support pagination. API supporting pagination have a special calling convention.</p><p>The parameters of the pagination api request are <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size</code> and <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code>. <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size</code> is the size of each page. Unless otherwise specified, the minimum value of <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size</code> is 1, the maximum value is 100, and the default value is 50. Setting <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size</code> to 0,  a negative number, or a number greater than 100 will result in an error.</p><p><code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> is used to locate the position (offset) of the pagination. Due to internal implementation reasons, the offset may not necessarily be a simple position number, but some internal data structure that can accurately locate the position. And the internal implementation of different api may be different. Therefore, those internal position data are encoded to <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> and returned  to developers.</p><p>When calling a paginated api for the first time, donot set <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> parameter or simply write <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token=</code>. This indicates that api should return the first page. For example:</p><pre class="hljs"><div class="copy-btn"><svg fill="currentColor" width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" If <code class="md-render_code-inline">has_more</code> is true, it must exist; otherwise, <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> will be an empty string.</li></ul><p>Use the returned <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> and keep other request parameters unchanged. Call the api again to get the data on the next page. If there is more data, a new <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> will be returned.</p><pre class="hljs"><div class="copy-btn"><svg fill="currentColor" width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" fill-rule="evenodd"><rect x="4" y="7" width="9" height="9" rx="1"></rect><path d="M8 4h7a1 1 0 011 1v7" stroke-linecap="round"></path></g></svg></div><code class="md-render_code-block"><div><div class="hljs-line" start="1">GET /task/v2/tasklist/:task_guid/tasks?page_size=10&page_token=Cg1UYXNrc1Rhc2tMaXN0EAMY.biLg5Mx</div></div></code></pre><p>Repeat this process until <code class="md-render_code-inline">has_more</code> is false. All data are retruend.  This is called a "traversal".</p><p>There are the following precautions when using the paging interface:</p><ul class="md_render-table_solid md_render-table"><li>During the repeated calls to the paging api, the data itself may change. For example, the original data list is A, B, C, D, E. Suppose you call the api with <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size=3</code> to get the first page A, B, C. Before calling the api next time, a new piece of data is inserted and placed after A, resulting in A, X, B, C, D, E. When you get the second page, you can only get D, E. X can only be obtained when you start over again from the first page.</li><li>During a traversal, do not modify any parameters other than page_token, including <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_size</code> and parameters for filtering data range. If you do this, you may get inaccurate paging results.</li><li>Always check the <code class="md-render_code-inline">has_more</code> field in the response. Only call the api to get the next page data when <code class="md-render_code-inline">has_more</code> is true. If you directly use the <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> in the response to initiate the next call, because the <code class="md-render_code-inline">page_token</code> of the last page is always an empty string, it will lead you back to the first page.</li></ul><h2 id="6134aee8" tabindex="-1">Idempotent Invocation</h2><p>Consider the following scenario: A third-party ticket system creates tasks associated with the ticket through the Create Task API. For example, for a ticket A, call Create Task API. It should create a task T, which is one-to-one associated with A. At the same time, the task creation also sets the "custom completion" function, allowing the task to automatically jump to the ticket A when the user clicks "complete" of T. However, the first invocation is timed out, so normally a retry was initiated to create the task. But in fact, the first timeout call has already taken effect, and a task has also been created. Therefore, 2 tasks are actually created, T1 and T2. But from the perspective of the ticket system, only T2 can be seen, and the relationship between A and T2 is established. In Lark App, however, both T1 and T2 tasks can be seen. Since T1 also has the "custom completion" function, clicking its "complete" will jump to ticket A. But if complete A, because A is only associated with T2, only T2 will be set to completed. This will result in a task T1 that can never be completed. To eliminate T1, the user can only choose to "exit task T1" or forcibly delete it manually.</p><p>When Lark system is under heavy load, there may be a large number of timeouts. It is impossible to determine how many times timeout occurred and how many duplicate tasks would be created.</p><p>To solve this problem, Idempotent processing is introduced. For example, for the Create Task API, in addition to filling in the regular task fields, you can also set the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> field. This field should be a string type that can uniquely determine the request source, such as the unique ID of ticket A in the above scenario. The Lark Task system guarantees that, when using the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> for a request within a time period, no matter how many times it is called, only one task will be created. This behavior is called idempotent invocation.</p><pre class="hljs"><div class="copy-btn"><svg fill="currentColor" width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" fill-rule="evenodd"><rect x="4" y="7" width="9" height="9" rx="1"></rect><path d="M8 4h7a1 1 0 011 1v7" stroke-linecap="round"></path></g></svg></div><code class="md-render_code-block"><div><div class="hljs-line" start="1">POST /task/v2/tasks</div><div class="hljs-line" start="2">{</div><div class="hljs-line" start="3">   "summary": "Idempotent task",</div><div class="hljs-line" start="4">   "client_token": "mBDlrQwWRkiuDckhFzoMy00l4026jK"</div><div class="hljs-line" start="5">}</div></div></code></pre><p>After invoking this api, if 500 Http Status Code is received, indicating an internal Error, the caller can wait for a while and retry the call with the same parameters until the interface is successful.</p><blockquote><p>If the maximum number of retries is exceeded and the 500 status code is still reported, and the error message does not provide a specific reason, you can provide feedback, and Lark developers will assist in troubleshooting the problem.</p></blockquote><p>Interfaces that currently support idempotent capabilities include: <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/create" class="internal-link" target="_self">Create Task</a>, <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task-subtask/create" class="internal-link" target="_self">Create Subtask</a>, and <a href="/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/task-v2/task/add_members" class="internal-link" target="_self">Add Task Members</a>. If you need other interfaces to support idempotent capabilities, please provide feedback.</p><p>Precautions for using idempotent capabilities:</p><ul class="md_render-table_solid md_render-table"><li><code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> should be globally unique. It is recommended to use the ID of the associated business data or generate it by UUID. Lark system interanally only perform basic string comparison on the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code>. The comparison is case-sensitive.</li><li>The parameters of requests using the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> must remain unchanged. When Lark system checks whether to perform idempotent behavior, it only checks the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> to determine whether it is the same request in business semantics, but not check the all request parameters. The behavior of an api request that uses the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> but provides different parameters is undefined. The correctness of such calls are not guaranteed.</li><li>When concurrently initiating multiple requests with the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> and completely identical parameters, only the first request to reach the server will be processed; the remaining requests will be automatically rejected and will receive an error code of <code class="md-render_code-inline">code:1470422</code>.</li><li>Idempotent behavior has isolation:<ul class="md_render-table_hollow md_render-table"><li>Idempotent behaviors between different api are isolated. For example, after calling api A using the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code>, call api B using the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code>. The call to api B will not be considered as an idempotent call to api A.</li><li>Idempotent behaviors between different callers are isolated. After access_token A uses the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> to call the api, access_token B uses the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code>  will not be considered as an idempotent call to access_token A and will not return the result of request from access_token A.</li></ul></li><li><code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> has a time limit. After it expires, calling the api with a previously used <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> will not get the result will be treated as a brand new <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code>. In simple terms, the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> cannot be used as a resource ID. The specific time limit of the <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> is:<ul class="md_render-table_hollow md_render-table"><li>If the api is actually successful, the idempotent behavior will last for 5 minutes. After it expires, the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> will also be treated as a new token. The "actual success" here means that the internal call is successful, but the caller has timed out due to the gateway settings of the open platform.</li><li>If the interface api fails, the same <code class="md-render_code-inline">client_token</code> will immediately be treated as a new token.</li></ul></li></ul></div></div><div class="feedback-word-btn-v2 feedback-word-btn-v2-hidden"><button
